fun_highlights: The prose quality is genuinely good and holds up across lives. Lines like 'Left the party before it turned' (Pavel Ashby, Dynasty 2), 'Was elsewhere as often as here, and the elsewhere was wide' (Linnea Salvedi, Dynasty 6), and 'Laughed easily to the end, in a way the hard years never quite explained' (Roman Lindholm, Dynasty 15) feel earned rather than generated. In 3-5 minute sessions, this prose is the primary reward and it delivers.

The vocation system creates genuinely different structural shapes. Comparing Henrik Brandt (maker: shop decision, masterwork, trade handoff) against Iris Brandt (scholar: study pays, legacy question, passing the question on) against Ronja Brandt (wanderer: restlessness, horizon, return) shows real divergence in which beats appear and in what order. A mobile snacker gets a different arc almost every life.

The callback mechanic — especially cb_books_late (Ren Salvedi reading the too-hard book at age 49), cb_lookaway (Niall Marchetti passing the rough sleeper at age 51), and cb_outcast_return — creates the genre's core pleasure: a distant early choice paying off decades later. These fire within a single session and are the single best reason to keep playing.

The era system gives each dynasty a different felt texture at zero extra reading cost. Dynasty 6 (Salvedi) opens in a war era and Ren's vocation card reads 'There is a war on, and it is hungry for the young' instead of the generic fork — immediate flavour in the first 10 seconds of a new session. Dynasty 11 (Okonkwo) has the plague era, which gates the epidemic-tending cards and changes how the marriage prompt reads. This is exactly the kind of variety a mobile snacker wants: different context, same format.

The dynasty layer's heirlooms and motto crystallization are punchy micro-rewards. Seeing 'The family's character has settled, at last, into words: Nothing was given; all was built' appear mid-session (Brandt, Dynasty 1, gen 3) gives a short burst of satisfaction. The heirloom list ('a book too hard for a child's hands', 'a soft spot for strays') accumulates across 5 minutes in a way that makes the dynasty feel real without requiring sustained attention.
staleness: The childhood checklist is highly predictable. In 15 dynasties, nearly every life runs the same opening sequence: c_origin -> c_wonder OR c_unfair OR c_dark -> c_sibling OR c_animal -> y_calling. Lives that are not meaningfully distinguished by era or trait run visibly parallel childhoods. Calla Brandt (gen 5) and Calla Okonkwo (gen 5) both hit c_unfair then c_animal (stray) in childhood before their callings — the same structural rhythm despite different names.

The mid-life body-decline sequence is templated to the point of being mechanical. In the transcripts, almost every life past age 40 hits one or more of the same stamped observations: 'Some mornings the body answers the bell late', 'The stairs have started to ask a question of them', 'The body has begun keeping its own quiet counsel', 'Mornings take longer to arrive in the body'. These are observe() pool entries, not cards, so they fire regardless of choices. In a short session spanning three lives, you will see two or three of these verbatim phrases. They are not bad writing but they are ambient wallpaper, and they accumulate into a predictable late-life texture.

The 'left home / went back' callback (cb_left_home) fires in Dynasty 1 (Ronja, age 52), Dynasty 6 (Anders, age 50 and 56), Dynasty 8 (Noor, age 48 and 67), Dynasty 11 (Naima, age 53), Dynasty 12 (Ottilie, age 58). That is five hits across 15 dynasties. The framing varies ('smaller than she remembered', 'went back to where she began') but the beat is identical — the returned wanderer finds the town shrunken. A mobile snacker cycling through dynasties will see this shape repeatedly, and the response options are essentially the same both times it fires in a single life (Anders at 50, then again at 56).

The marriage and child beats are structurally repetitive even with varied prose. The a_marry prompt appears in 13 of 15 dynasties with essentially identical trigger logic: love exists, not yet married, cooldown elapsed. The prose variants ('a quiet certainty for years', 'fell asleep first again', 'only the small enormous matter of saying the words out loud') are good, but the dramatic shape — hesitation, then commitment or refusal — is the same each time. Across 3 lives in a session the player has made this choice 3 times in a row, always between 'Ask. Build a life.' and 'Not yet. Maybe never.' A mobile snacker notices this.

The e_bequest card fires in Dynasty 1 (Carys, age 64), Dynasty 2 (Greta, age 60), Dynasty 6 (Linnea, age 65), Dynasty 11 (Yara, age 78), Dynasty 15 (Roman, implied). The four choices never change and the framing ('There is still time to set aside one thing, deliberately, for them') is identical every time. The option text ('Everything I know', 'Every coin I can spare', 'The stories, and the warmth', 'Nothing but their own freedom') doesn't even vary. This is the genre's natural succession-handoff moment but it's the most mechanically repetitive card in the game — a mobile snacker who plays several dynasties will see it 3-5 times and it will never surprise them.

Epitaph variety is thinner than it appears. Despite the anti-repetition logic in dynasty.js (blocked() by cluster, RECENT_CLUSTERS, RECENT_LINES), the transcripts show clustering: 'Taught what she knew, and so outlived the knowing of it' appears for Lazlo Bjornsen (Dynasty 5) and Linnea Okonkwo (Dynasty 11). 'Left people gentler than they found them' appears for Anders Salvedi (Dynasty 6) and Noor Ashby (Dynasty 8). 'Kind in the small daily ways that turn out to be the large ones' appears for Edmund Ashby (Dynasty 2) and Theda Quint (Dynasty 12). In a continuous session reading many dynasties, the player notices these repetitions, which undercuts the sense that each life ended as its own unique thing.

improvements.what: Give e_bequest varied framing across generations, and add at least 2-3 new option texts that reflect the specific life just lived (e.g. a soldier's version that mentions the blade, a wanderer's that mentions the road). The card fires every generation in a multi-gen dynasty and its four frozen options are word-for-word identical every time.
improvements.why: This is the most templated card in the game by far. A mobile snacker hitting it in generation 2, 3, and 4 of the same dynasty sees identical text three times in a row. Even light variation ('Everything I know — the long scholarship of it' for a scholar, 'Everything I can spare — and I earned every coin' for a maker) would break the repetition.

improvements.what: Add 2-3 more childhood structural divergence paths so a bookish child and a restless child don't run the same 4-beat sequence. The trait affinity system in engine.js (TRAIT_AFFINITY weights c_book toward 'bookish', c_friend toward 'warm') is the right mechanism but the pool is thin — there are only ~8 childhood cards and most aren't trait-gated. Add 1-2 cards exclusive to specific trait combos (a 'dreaming' child gets a different wonder card; a 'stubborn' child gets a conflict card that bookish doesn't).
improvements.why: The jury's brief specifically names childhood staleness. The transcripts confirm it: Calla Brandt gen 5 and Calla Okonkwo gen 5 have near-identical childhood structures. Trait affinity exists but doesn't create enough divergence because there aren't enough trait-exclusive cards.

improvements.what: Reduce the frequency of the cb_left_home / wanderer-return beat, or add a third framing for a character who has returned once and is asked again (it fires twice in the same life for Anders Salvedi at 50 and 56, with nearly identical prompt text). The second firing in the same life should acknowledge the prior return explicitly ('You went back once, at 50. The question comes again.').
improvements.why: In Dynasty 6, Anders is asked the same return-to-hometown question twice 6 years apart. The second prompt ('After all the years and all the roads, Anders comes back to the place he started') is nearly identical to the first. The player has just made this choice; the repeat feels like a bug.

improvements.what: Add one or two era-specific adult cards for the 'war' era beyond the vocation-gate variation. Right now a war era mostly affects the y_calling prompt text and adds the a_marry urgency framing, but a non-soldier adult in a war era plays identically to a settled-era adult. A card like 'the house two doors down has lost someone; the war comes to your street' would make the era feel like more than a label.
improvements.why: The era system promises 'gen 8 is not gen 2 with new names' (engine.js comment) but in practice only the opening line and the vocation card see war-specific text. A wanderer or scholar in a war era never faces a war-specific dilemma. Given how good the era framing already is, this is easy to extend.

improvements.what: Trim or pool the body-decline observe() lines more aggressively across a session (not just within a life). The current logic fires each observation at most once PER LIFE but the same line can recur across lives in the same session. A session-level RECENT_LINES guard (which already exists for epitaphs) should be applied to observe() outputs, or the pool should be large enough (it's currently 10 lines per condition) that repetition is rare.
improvements.why: A mobile snacker playing 3 lives sees mid-life body-decline observations 6-8 times. The pool rotation means they will hear the same phrasing again, and these are ambient background lines — not choices — so they have nothing to do except register as wallpaper. The epitaph system already has the right solution (RECENT_LINES global dedup); applying it to observe() would cost almost nothing.

verdict: A Life is a genuinely well-written game with real structural variation and a callback mechanic that delivers the genre's best pleasure cleanly in a short session. For a mobile snacker, the prose quality and vocation-shaped divergence earn real goodwill in the first 10-15 minutes. The problem is the second and third dynasties: the childhood checklist, the frozen e_bequest options, the body-decline observation wallpaper, and the marriage/return beats start showing their templates in exactly the 15-30 minute window where a mobile snacker decides whether to keep the app. The engine has all the right mechanisms — the trait affinity system, era gating, callback reach-back, epitaph dedup — and most of the staleness problems are fixable by extending existing patterns rather than rebuilding anything. At its current state it scores just above the staleness-dominates threshold, held there by the quality of its best moments.
